subject.title: RFC: Per-session tool policies — bridging operator scopes and agent tool access

question: Should OpenClaw define an operator-scope-aware runtime tool-policy layer, and if so should that policy live in agent config, gateway config, or a broader tenant/session authorization model?
rationale: This changes the meaning of gateway scopes from method access into tool-execution authorization and could imply security guarantees across sessions or users, so automation cannot choose the trust boundary or config precedence safely.

options.title: Design Scope-Aware Tool Policy
options.body: Keep this issue open and approve a narrow design for scope-to-tool-policy precedence, enforcement layer, docs, and upgrade tests before implementation.

options.title: Route To Sender Or Tenant Work
options.body: Treat operator scopes as the wrong primitive and move the remaining work to sender/group policies, session envelopes, or the broader tenant-RBAC tracker.

options.title: Decline Scope Bridge For Now
options.body: Document separate gateways, trusted proxy identity, sender policies, and per-agent profiles as the supported isolation path without adding `toolsByScope`.

recommendation.title: Design Scope-Aware Tool Policy
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and approve a narrow design for scope-to-tool-policy precedence, enforcement layer, docs, and upgrade tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history signal is around scoped conversation profiles and the Gateway trust-model/security docs that frame this decision.
